quantity.definition: the number of ciphertexts decapsulable under ONE ML-KEM encapsulation key
quantity.scope_restriction: This census reports M and nothing derived from M. No bit figure, no log2 M, no G appears anywhere in this artifact, per the task card.

distribution_sentence: Across the 14 deployment-mode rows sourced here, 6 fix M = 1 (R09, R12, R14, R20, R21, R22) and the remaining 8 state no count bound at all (R06, R10, R15, R16, R17, R18, R19, R23) -- and the largest numeric M stated by ANY of the 24 rows, ephemeral or static, is 1, because every static row bounds the key in time or by a rate-limiting SHOULD and never by a number of ciphertexts.
does_any_standardised_mode_state_M_above: No retrieved specification states any numeric M greater than 1, so none states an M above 2^20. Symmetrically, and this must be reported with equal weight: none of the 8 count-unstated modes forbids one either. The absence is an absence of a stated number in both directions; it is not a sourced ceiling and must not be read as one.

rows.spec: FIPS 203 (NIST, final, 2024-08-13)
rows.section: Announcement point 13; Sec. 3.3 (Requirements for ML-KEM Implementations); Sec. 7.1 (ML-KEM Key Generation)
rows.bounding_mechanism: NONE. FIPS 203 fixes no lifetime, cryptoperiod, use counter or decapsulation limit for a (ek, dk) pair. Sec. 3.3 states that 'Additional requirements, including requirements for using ML-KEM in specific applications, are given in SP 800-227', and Sec. 7.1 says only that dk 'shall remain private'.
rows.m_derivation: Full-text search of the retrieved PDF for 'cryptoperiod', 'number of (queries|decapsulations|encapsulations|ciphertexts|uses)', 'multi-user', 'multi-target', 'at most 2', 'single use', 'one-time' returns no use-count bound; the only matches for 'destroy' concern intermediate values and the shared secret. M is therefore delegated entirely to the deploying specification.
rows.citation: NIST, FIPS 203, Module-Lattice-Based Key-Encapsulation Mechanism Standard, 2024-08-13, https://nvlpubs.nist.gov/nistpubs/FIPS/NIST.FIPS.203.pdf

rows.spec: NIST SP 800-227 (Recommendations for KEMs, September 2025)
rows.section: Sec. 4.2 'KEM key-pair usage'; requirement RS6
rows.bounding_mechanism: Normative single-use rule: 'If an application uses an ephemeral key pair, the key pair shall be used for only one execution of key-establishment via a KEM and shall be destroyed as soon as possible after its use.'
rows.m_derivation: One execution of key-establishment admits exactly one ciphertext, so M = 1 directly from the 'shall'.
rows.citation: NIST SP 800-227, Recommendations for Key-Encapsulation Mechanisms, September 2025, https://nvlpubs.nist.gov/nistpubs/SpecialPublications/NIST.SP.800-227.pdf

rows.spec: NIST SP 800-227 (Recommendations for KEMs, September 2025)
rows.section: Sec. 4.1 'Static versus ephemeral key pairs'; Sec. 4.2 requirement RM3
rows.bounding_mechanism: Explicitly unbounded in count: 'Alice might then accept many connections from multiple parties over a long period of time, each initiated via ek_A. ... In this scenario, Alice's encapsulation key is said to be static.' The only requirement attached to the static case (RM3) is ownership assurance, not a use count.
rows.m: not stated ('many connections ... over a long period of time')
rows.m_derivation: The clause is qualitative. Full-text search of SP 800-227 for 'number of (queries|decapsulations|encapsulations|ciphertexts|uses)', 'multi-user', 'multi-target', 'limit the number' and 'cryptoperiod' returns zero matches, so this document supplies no count and no time bound for the static case.
rows.citation: NIST SP 800-227, Sec. 4.1-4.2, September 2025

rows.spec: NIST SP 800-57 Part 1 Rev. 5
rows.section: Sec. 5.3.6, Table 1, rows 15 and 16 (Private / Public Ephemeral Key Agreement Key)
rows.bounding_mechanism: Cryptoperiod stated as a transaction count: 'One key-agreement transaction'.
rows.m_derivation: The cryptoperiod is itself the count: one transaction, hence one ciphertext, hence M = 1.
rows.citation: NIST SP 800-57 Part 1 Rev. 5, Recommendation for Key Management, Sec. 5.3.6 Table 1, https://nvlpubs.nist.gov/nistpubs/SpecialPublications/NIST.SP.800-57pt1r5.pdf

rows.spec: NIST SP 800-57 Part 1 Rev. 5
rows.section: Sec. 5.3.6, Table 1, rows 13 and 14 (Private / Public Static Key Agreement Key)
rows.bounding_mechanism: TIME bound only: cryptoperiod '1 to 2 years'. The narrative for row 13 says a private static key-agreement key 'may be used multiple times' and that its cryptoperiod ends at the notAfter date of the last certificate issued for the corresponding public key.
rows.m: not stated as a count; bounded only in time (1 to 2 years)
rows.m_derivation: Converting '1 to 2 years' into a ciphertext count requires a decapsulation rate. No retrieved specification supplies one, so no count is derived here. Recording the rate as an assumption would be an estimate presented as a source, which rule 9 forbids.
rows.citation: NIST SP 800-57 Part 1 Rev. 5, Sec. 5.3.6 Table 1 rows 13-14

rows.spec: RFC 9180 (HPKE) - base and PSK modes, recipient KEM key pair
rows.section: Sec. 9.2.3 'KEM Key Reuse'; Sec. 9.7.4 'Forward Secrecy'
rows.bounding_mechanism: No count bound. Sec. 9.2.3 forbids reuse of DeriveKeyPair ikm and of Encap randomness, and then explicitly permits recipient key-pair reuse: 'Since a KEM key pair belonging to a sender or recipient works with all modes, it can be used with multiple modes in parallel.' Sec. 9.7.4 states the recipient side uses only long-term secrets.
rows.m_derivation: The only 'MUST NOT reuse' clauses in RFC 9180 bind ikm and encapsulation randomness, i.e. the SENDER side, never the number of ciphertexts a recipient key may decapsulate.
rows.citation: RFC 9180, Hybrid Public Key Encryption, February 2022, https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9180.txt

rows.spec: RFC 9180 (HPKE) - auth and auth_psk modes
rows.section: RFC 9180 Sec. 5.1.3-5.1.4; draft-connolly-cfrg-hpke-mlkem-04 Sec. 1.2 and Sec. 3.7
rows.bounding_mechanism: Inapplicable to ML-KEM. 'ML-KEM is a plain KEM that does not support the static-static key agreement needed by ... their (optional) authenticated modes' and 'HPKE-ML-KEM is not an authenticated KEM and does not support AuthEncap() nor AuthDecap()'.
rows.m: n/a - ML-KEM cannot instantiate HPKE auth/auth_psk
rows.m_derivation: Recorded because the task card lists HPKE auth mode; the mode carries no ML-KEM M because ML-KEM cannot serve it.
rows.citation: draft-connolly-cfrg-hpke-mlkem-04, Sec. 1.2, 3.7, https://www.ietf.org/archive/id/draft-connolly-cfrg-hpke-mlkem-04.txt

rows.spec: HPKE ML-KEM bindings (draft-connolly-cfrg-hpke-mlkem-04; draft-ietf-hpke-pq-04)
rows.section: IANA 'HPKE KEM Identifiers': 0x0040/0x0041/0x0042 = ML-KEM-512/768/1024; 0x0050 MLKEM768-P256; 0x0051 MLKEM1024-P384; 0x647A X-Wing. draft-connolly-cfrg-hpke-mlkem-04 Sec. 4 (Security Considerations)
rows.bounding_mechanism: No count bound. The bindings register ML-KEM as an HPKE KEM and discuss binding properties (MAL-BIND-K-CT, LEAK-BIND-K-PK); neither draft states a limit on decapsulations under one recipient key.
rows.m_derivation: Full-text search of both drafts for 'reuse', 'number of' and 'limit' returns no per-key use bound.
rows.citation: IANA, Hybrid Public Key Encryption (HPKE) IANA registry, 'HPKE KEM Identifiers', https://www.iana.org/assignments/hpke/hpke.xhtml; draft-ietf-hpke-pq-04; draft-connolly-cfrg-hpke-mlkem-04

rows.spec: RFC 9420 (MLS) - KeyPackage init_key
rows.section: Sec. 10 'Key Packages'; Sec. 16.8 'KeyPackage Reuse'
rows.bounding_mechanism: Single-use SHOULD: 'KeyPackages are intended to be used only once and SHOULD NOT be reused except in the case of a "last resort" KeyPackage'; Sec. 16.8: 'once a KeyPackage has been used ... it SHOULD be deleted from the KeyPackage publication system.' init_key 'MUST be unique among the set of KeyPackages created by this client'.
rows.m_derivation: One KeyPackage carries one init_key and admits one Welcome ciphertext (Sec. 12.4.3.1 EncryptWithLabel(init_key, 'Welcome', ...)), so M = 1 under the SHOULD. Recorded as SHOULD, not MUST.
rows.citation: RFC 9420, The Messaging Layer Security (MLS) Protocol, July 2023, https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9420.txt

rows.spec: RFC 9420 (MLS) + draft-ietf-mls-extensions-10 - last-resort KeyPackage
rows.section: RFC 9420 Sec. 16.8; draft-ietf-mls-extensions-10 Sec. 6.4 'Last-Resort KeyPackages'; RFC 9420 Sec. 7.2 (LeafNode Lifetime)
rows.bounding_mechanism: Reuse explicitly permitted with NO count: 'An application MAY allow for reuse of a "last resort" KeyPackage in order to prevent denial-of-service attacks'; the extension marks KeyPackages 'that MAY be used more than once'. The only bounds offered are a rate-limiting SHOULD on the Delivery Service (Sec. 16.8) and the LeafNode Lifetime not_before/not_after time window (Sec. 7.2).
rows.m: not stated as a count; bounded only by a rate-limiting SHOULD and the LeafNode Lifetime window
rows.m_derivation: Neither RFC 9420 nor the extensions draft states any number; a count would require a rate and a window that the deployer, not the specification, fixes.
rows.citation: RFC 9420 Sec. 16.8; draft-ietf-mls-extensions-10, Sec. 6.4, https://www.ietf.org/archive/id/draft-ietf-mls-extensions-10.txt

rows.spec: RFC 9420 (MLS) - cipher suite registry
rows.section: Sec. 17.1, 'MLS Cipher Suites' table (values 0x0001-0x0007)
rows.bounding_mechanism: RFC 9420 as published registers only DHKEM(X25519), DHKEM(X448), DHKEM(P-256), DHKEM(P-384) and DHKEM(P-521) cipher suites. Full-text search for 'ML-KEM'/'MLKEM' in RFC 9420 returns no match.
rows.m: n/a - no ML-KEM cipher suite is standardised in RFC 9420
rows.m_derivation: Recorded so that R09/R10 are not read as standardised ML-KEM deployments; they are the KeyPackage MECHANISM, which an ML-KEM MLS cipher suite would inherit.

rows.spec: TLS 1.3 hybrid key_share, X25519MLKEM768 (draft-ietf-tls-ecdhe-mlkem-05, in the RFC Editor queue as RFC-ietf-tls-ecdhe-mlkem-05)
rows.section: Sec. 4.1 'Client share'; Sec. 4.2 'Server share'; Sec. 6 'Security Considerations'
rows.key_role: ephemeral (client-generated ML-KEM encapsulation key in the ClientHello key_share)
rows.bounding_mechanism: Message structure: the client's key_share carries one ML-KEM-768 encapsulation key and the server's key_share carries exactly one ciphertext, so one handshake yields one decapsulation. The draft itself imposes no freshness rule; its Sec. 6 defers to draft-ietf-tls-hybrid-design and to NIST SP 800-227.
rows.m_derivation: One ServerHello key_share ciphertext per offered client share. This is structural, not a normative single-use rule: see R13 for the governing reuse clause, which permits key-share reuse.
rows.citation: draft-ietf-tls-ecdhe-mlkem-05, Post-quantum hybrid ECDHE-MLKEM Key Agreement for TLSv1.3, https://www.ietf.org/archive/id/draft-ietf-tls-ecdhe-mlkem-05.txt; IANA TLS Supported Groups value 4588 X25519MLKEM768

rows.spec: draft-ietf-tls-hybrid-design-16 (the reuse clause governing R12 and R14)
rows.section: Sec. 2 'Key encapsulation mechanisms'
rows.key_role: ephemeral or reused, at the implementation's choice
rows.bounding_mechanism: Reuse permitted, bound DELEGATED: 'TLS 1.3 does not require that ephemeral public keys be used only in a single key exchange session; some implementations may reuse them ... While it is recommended that implementations avoid reuse of KEM public keys, implementations that do reuse KEM public keys MUST ensure that the number of reuses of a KEM public key abides by any bounds in the specification of the KEM or subsequent security analyses.'
rows.m: not stated; delegated to 'any bounds in the specification of the KEM', and FIPS 203 states none (R01)
rows.m_derivation: This is the load-bearing chain for TLS: the only normative pointer to a numeric M points at FIPS 203, and R01 records that FIPS 203 contains no such number. The delegation therefore terminates without a value.
rows.citation: draft-ietf-tls-hybrid-design-16, Hybrid key exchange in TLS 1.3, Sec. 2, https://www.ietf.org/archive/id/draft-ietf-tls-hybrid-design-16.txt

rows.spec: TLS 1.3 standalone ML-KEM key agreement (draft-connolly-tls-mlkem-key-agreement-05; IANA groups 512/513/514 MLKEM512/768/1024)
rows.section: Sec. 4.2 'Transmitting encapsulation keys and ciphertexts'; Sec. 6.2 'IND-CCA'
rows.bounding_mechanism: Same structure and same delegation as R12/R13: one server ciphertext per client encapsulation key, and Sec. 6.2 repeats verbatim that reusing implementations 'MUST ensure that the number of reuses of a KEM public key abides by any bounds in the specification of the KEM'.
rows.m_derivation: Structural, as R12. The delegated reuse bound terminates at FIPS 203, which states none.
rows.citation: draft-connolly-tls-mlkem-key-agreement-05, https://www.ietf.org/archive/id/draft-connolly-tls-mlkem-key-agreement-05.txt; IANA TLS Supported Groups values 512-514

rows.spec: TLS Encrypted Client Hello (draft-ietf-tls-esni-25) - ECHConfig HPKE key
rows.section: Sec. 4 'Encrypted ClientHello Configuration'; Sec. 10.3 'Client Tracking'; Sec. 10.10.5 'Maintain Forward Secrecy'; Sec. 9 'Compliance Requirements'
rows.bounding_mechanism: Static key with a rotation RECOMMENDATION and no count: 'This design does not provide forward secrecy for the inner ClientHello because the server's ECH key is static. However, the window of exposure is bound by the key lifetime. It is RECOMMENDED that servers rotate keys regularly.' Sec. 10.3 pushes the other way: 'Rotating too frequently limits the client anonymity set ... anonymity sets will typically involve many connections even with fairly fast rotation intervals.'
rows.m: not stated as a count; bounded only by a rotation RECOMMENDATION, and the privacy goal argues for a LARGE number of connections per config
rows.m_derivation: No number appears. This is the one surveyed mode whose own privacy goal actively rewards a larger M, so it is the natural place to look for a large deployed value; the specification still supplies none. Note also Sec. 9: the mandatory-to-implement KEM is DHKEM(X25519, HKDF-SHA256), so an ML-KEM ECH deployment would use the registered ML-KEM HPKE KEM ids of R08 rather than anything ECH itself standardises.
rows.citation: draft-ietf-tls-esni-25, TLS Encrypted Client Hello, 14 June 2025, https://www.ietf.org/archive/id/draft-ietf-tls-esni-25.txt

rows.spec: X-Wing hybrid KEM (draft-connolly-cfrg-xwing-kem-10)
rows.section: Sec. 1.4 'Not an authenticated KEM'; Sec. 6 'Security Considerations'; Sec. 6.1 'Binding properties'
rows.bounding_mechanism: No count bound. The draft states the IND-CCA reduction to ML-KEM-768 and gap-CDH for Curve25519 and lists binding properties; it fixes no key lifetime, no rotation rule and no use counter.
rows.m_derivation: Full-text search of the draft for 'reuse', 'once', 'number of', 'static' and 'limit' returns no per-key use bound. X-Wing is registered as HPKE KEM id 0x647A, so R06's HPKE recipient-key situation applies to it.
rows.citation: draft-connolly-cfrg-xwing-kem-10, X-Wing: general-purpose hybrid post-quantum KEM, March 2026, https://www.ietf.org/archive/id/draft-connolly-cfrg-xwing-kem-10.txt

rows.spec: LAMPS PQ certificate profile: ML-KEM in X.509 (draft-ietf-lamps-kyber-certificates-11)
rows.section: Sec. 1.1 'Applicability Statement'; Sec. 5 'Key Usage Bits'; Sec. 9 'Security Considerations'
rows.bounding_mechanism: Certificate validity only. The profile fixes algorithm identifiers, the SubjectPublicKeyInfo encoding, the private key format and keyEncipherment as the only permitted key usage; it states no decapsulation count, and Sec. 9 refers key-reuse questions out to draft-sfluhrer-cfrg-ml-kem-security-considerations (R24).
rows.m: not stated as a count; bounded only by the certificate validity period (RFC 5280 notBefore/notAfter), for which SP 800-57 Part 1 Rev. 5 suggests 1 to 2 years (R05)
rows.m_derivation: No count appears in the profile. Converting the validity period into a count needs a decapsulation rate that no retrieved specification supplies.
rows.citation: draft-ietf-lamps-kyber-certificates-11, Algorithm Identifiers for ML-KEM in X.509, https://www.ietf.org/archive/id/draft-ietf-lamps-kyber-certificates-11.txt

rows.spec: CMS KEMRecipientInfo (RFC 9629) with ML-KEM (draft-ietf-lamps-cms-kyber-13)
rows.section: RFC 9629 Sec. 7 'Security Considerations'; draft-ietf-lamps-cms-kyber-13 Sec. 2.3 'Certificate Conventions'
rows.key_role: static (recipient key from a long-lived certificate)
rows.bounding_mechanism: Unbounded by design and stated as such: 'the KEM algorithm MUST explicitly be designed to be secure when the public key is used many times. For example, a KEM algorithm with a single-use public key is not appropriate, because the public key is expected to be carried in a long-lived certificate and used over and over.' One KEM ciphertext per recipient per message; a message count is never fixed.
rows.m: not stated; the specification's explicit intent is 'used over and over' (one ciphertext per protected message per recipient)
rows.m_derivation: RFC 9629's own 'MUST NOT be reused' clauses bind the IKM and the encapsulation randomness, i.e. per-message sender-side values, never the recipient key's use count.
rows.citation: RFC 9629, Using Key Encapsulation Mechanism (KEM) Algorithms in CMS, August 2024, https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9629.txt; draft-ietf-lamps-cms-kyber-13, https://www.ietf.org/archive/id/draft-ietf-lamps-cms-kyber-13.txt

rows.spec: HSM / embedded profile: PKCS#11 v3.2 (OASIS, OS) ML-KEM mechanisms
rows.section: Sec. 6.68 'ML-KEM' (CKK_ML_KEM, CKM_ML_KEM_KEY_PAIR_GEN, CKM_ML_KEM); C_DecapsulateKey; object attributes CKA_TOKEN, CKA_DECAPSULATE
rows.key_role: static (token object persisting in the module)
rows.bounding_mechanism: None. An ML-KEM private key object with CKA_TOKEN = CK_TRUE persists in the token across sessions, and CKA_DECAPSULATE is a plain boolean gating C_DecapsulateKey. There is no usage counter attribute.
rows.m_derivation: Full-text search of the retrieved specification for 'CKA_USAGE', 'usage count' and 'usage limit' returns 0 matches, so the API exposes no way for the module to cap the number of decapsulations under one key.
rows.citation: OASIS, PKCS #11 Specification Version 3.2 (OASIS Standard), Sec. 6.68, https://docs.oasis-open.org/pkcs11/pkcs11-spec/v3.2/os/pkcs11-spec-v3.2-os.html

rows.spec: SSH PQ/T hybrid key exchange with ML-KEM (draft-ietf-sshm-mlkem-hybrid-kex-10)
rows.section: Sec. 6 'Security Considerations'
rows.bounding_mechanism: Normative per-connection freshness: 'generating an ephemeral key exchange keypair for ECDH and ML-KEM per connection is REQUIRED by this specification.'
rows.m_derivation: One keypair per connection and one server ciphertext per connection, so M = 1 under the REQUIRED.
rows.citation: draft-ietf-sshm-mlkem-hybrid-kex-10, PQ/T Hybrid Key Exchange with ML-KEM in SSH, https://www.ietf.org/archive/id/draft-ietf-sshm-mlkem-hybrid-kex-10.txt

rows.spec: IKEv2 post-quantum key exchange with ML-KEM (draft-ietf-ipsecme-ikev2-mlkem-09)
rows.section: Sec. 3 'Security Considerations'
rows.bounding_mechanism: Normative per-exchange freshness: 'Generating an ephemeral keypair and ciphertext for each ML-KEM key exchange is REQUIRED by this specification.'
rows.m_derivation: One keypair per key exchange and one responder ciphertext per exchange, so M = 1 under the REQUIRED.
rows.citation: draft-ietf-ipsecme-ikev2-mlkem-09, Post-quantum Key Exchange with ML-KEM in IKEv2, https://www.ietf.org/archive/id/draft-ietf-ipsecme-ikev2-mlkem-09.txt

rows.spec: Signal PQXDH (deployed) - one-time pqkem prekey PQOPK_B
rows.section: Sec. 2.5 'Post-Quantum Key Encapsulation Keys'; Sec. 3.2 'Publishing keys'
rows.bounding_mechanism: Single-use by definition: 'a set of signed one-time prekeys (PQOPK_B1, PQOPK_B2, ...) which are also signed with IK_B and each used in a single PQXDH protocol run.'
rows.m_derivation: One protocol run consumes one prekey and carries one KEM ciphertext, so M = 1.
rows.citation: Signal, The PQXDH Key Agreement Protocol, Sec. 2.5, 3.2, https://signal.org/docs/specifications/pqxdh/
rows.caveat: PQXDH's pqkem parameter is specified as 'a post-quantum key encapsulation mechanism that has IND-CCA post-quantum security (e.g. Crystals-Kyber-1024)'. The retrieved specification text names Kyber-1024, not FIPS 203 ML-KEM. Included as a DEPLOYED KEM profile whose M-bounding mechanism is the object of interest; do not read it as an ML-KEM conformance statement.

rows.spec: Signal PQXDH (deployed) - signed last-resort pqkem prekey PQSPK_B
rows.section: Sec. 2.5 'Post-Quantum Key Encapsulation Keys'; Sec. 3.2 'Publishing keys'
rows.bounding_mechanism: Rotation with no count: 'Bob has a signed last-resort post-quantum prekey PQSPK_B, which he changes periodically'. It is consumed 'when one-time pqkem prekeys are not available ... when the number of prekey bundles downloaded for Bob exceeds the number of one-time pqkem prekeys Bob has uploaded.'
rows.m: not stated; 'changes periodically', with the number of runs falling to it set by prekey-bundle demand versus one-time prekey supply
rows.m_derivation: The specification names the two quantities that determine M (bundle download rate, one-time prekey supply) and fixes neither. No count is derived here.
rows.citation: Signal, The PQXDH Key Agreement Protocol, Sec. 2.5, 3.2, https://signal.org/docs/specifications/pqxdh/
rows.caveat: Same Kyber-1024 versus FIPS 203 ML-KEM caveat as R22.

rows.spec: draft-sfluhrer-cfrg-ml-kem-security-considerations-05 (the CFRG statement the LAMPS profile defers to)
rows.section: Sec. 4 'ML-KEM Security Considerations'
rows.bounding_mechanism: Reuse endorsed without a count: 'It is secure to reuse a public key multiple times. That is, instead of Alice generating a fresh public and private keypair for each exchange, Alice may generate a public key once, and then publish that public key, and use it for multiple incoming ciphertexts, generating multiple shared secret keys. While this is safe, it is recommended that ... they should generate a fresh keypair each time ... to obtain Perfect Forward Secrecy.'
rows.m_derivation: This is where R17's Sec. 9 deferral lands, and it too terminates without a number. Full-text search of the draft for 'number of', 'limit' and '2^' returns no per-key use bound.
rows.citation: draft-sfluhrer-cfrg-ml-kem-security-considerations-05, ML-KEM Security Considerations, May 2026, https://www.ietf.org/archive/id/draft-sfluhrer-cfrg-ml-kem-security-considerations-05.txt
